newsitem.title: USA: New Haven mayor seeks Housing Authority overhaul.
newsitem.headline: New Haven mayor seeks Housing Authority overhaul.

text.p: New Haven Mayor John DeStefano, Jr. on Wednesday called for a reorganization of the troubled Housing Authority of New Haven, the state's largest housing authority with some 3,100 units.
He told a news conference that a national search for a new executive director of the housing authority would start immediately.
The new director will replace Bryan Anderson, whose contract expires at the end of June.
Quadel Consulting Corp of Washington, D.C., will act as interim manager of the housing authority, DeStefano said.
The mayor said the imminent collapse of the $45 million HOPE VI Elm Haven project persuaded him to take action.
The project's developer on Monday threatened to pull out of New Haven because of contract problems with the housing authority.
The housing authority has been plagued by serious financial and operational problems for some time.
"Enough is enough," DeStefano said. "As mayor of the city of New Haven, I can no longer tolerate the lack of action and direction on the part of the New Haven Housing Authority."
DeStefano said it was time "to be accountable to the taxpayers who underwrite the cost of public housing."
He said he would resist calls for the housing authority to be taken over by the Department of Housing and Urban Development.
"It's my intent to see that this housing authority remains under local control, because only we can solve our own problems," he said.
